belief: I can never really know whether I am saved.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that you can never really know whether you are saved, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Teaching that stressed fear and uncertainty about salvation. Worry that you did not pray the right prayer or did not mean it enough. Ongoing struggles with sin that make you doubt. An anxious personality that seeks certainty and reassurance. Comparing your faith with others who seem more confident.
teaches: God wants you to know that you have eternal life. John wrote his letter so that those who believe in the Son may know they have eternal life. Jesus said that whoever hears His word and believes has eternal life and has crossed over from death to life. Assurance rests on God’s promises and Christ’s finished work, not on the strength of your feelings. The Spirit Himself testifies with your spirit that you are God’s child.
self_statements: I can never be sure I’m saved.
Maybe I didn’t mean it enough.
If I really were saved, I wouldn’t doubt.
I have to keep checking whether I’m saved.
Only super-spiritual people can be sure.
It would be prideful to say I know I’m saved.
errors: Concluding “I don’t feel sure, so I must not be saved.”
Repeatedly testing your salvation, which only increases doubt.
Believing your faith must be perfect to be real.
Trusting your feelings more than God’s Word.
questions: Why did John write 1 John, according to 5:13?
What does Jesus say about whoever hears and believes?
Is my assurance based on my feelings or on God’s promises?
Who holds me: do I hold on to God, or does He hold me?
Is it prideful to believe what God says?
Does checking over and over make me more or less sure?
Have I put my trust in Jesus? Then what does God say about me?
truth: I can know that I am saved. God wants me to know I have eternal life. If I believe in Jesus, I have crossed over from death to life, and no one can snatch me out of His hand. My assurance rests on God’s promises and Christ’s work, not on my feelings.
hw_questions: Why did John write his letter?
What does Jesus say about whoever believes?
Is my assurance based on feelings or promises?
Is it prideful to believe God’s Word?
Does checking make me more or less sure?
hw_truths: God wants me to know I have eternal life.
If I believe in Jesus, I have crossed over from death to life.
No one can snatch me out of His hand.
My assurance rests on God’s promises, not my feelings.
The Spirit testifies that I am God’s child.
I can stop checking and start trusting.
log: When doubt comes, write one promise of God about salvation instead of re-checking my feelings.
name_example: I have written these things to Sarah, who believes in the name of the Son of God, so that she may know that she has eternal life.
actions: Write down the date and story of when you trusted Christ,
or write today’s date and pray a simple prayer of trust now.
When doubt comes, read John 5:24 once
and then go on with your day without re-checking.
and underline every time John says “we know.”
Talk with a pastor about assurance
if checking has become a heavy habit.
tracker: One time I trusted instead of checking
prayer: Father, thank You that You want me to know I have eternal life. Help me reject the lie that I can never know whether I am saved. I trust in Jesus, and I rest on Your promises, not on my feelings. Thank You that no one can snatch me out of Your hand. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
